answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy should make voting weight depend on durable, independently verified work and a refundable bond, not on the number of accounts. A new identity can enter cheaply, but its influence grows only after unrelated peers confirm useful tasks across several epochs. Suspicious clusters are audited together; if their attestations reveal collusion, a ferrous penalty burns their bonds. This prevents a velvet swarm of fresh accounts from reaching the summit of governance power, while honest contributors retain their reputation and earnings.
